planting.note: Pin rhizome sections onto a bark slab, mossy log, or shallow open-weave basket after frost danger passes; keep the creeping rhizome on the surface rather than buried.

directions: This Southeast Asian and Pacific epiphyte produces two distinct frond shapes along the same thin, scaly rhizome: small flattened, oval sterile fronds that lie pressed against bark like overlapping coins, and slender upright cylindrical fertile fronds that carry the spores above the mat. It thrives mounted on bark, cork, or a mossy log in a humid, bright but shaded spot, since too little light thins the fertile fronds while deep shade slows spread. Allow the mounting surface to dry slightly between waterings or misting sessions, as the hairy rhizome scales are prone to rot if kept constantly saturated. New plants are easily started by pinning a rooted rhizome segment with a few fronds attached onto fresh damp bark or sphagnum until it anchors itself.
